answer.justification: Only output-level data is available. Exact match (0.031), median first divergence (8) and edit distance (0.562) rule out none and both system-prompt classes, which diverge at token 0 with edit distance about 0.80. They fit the weight-change classes, so the text rates must decide. Fine-tune backdoor is disfavored: it should drop refusals (about 3 per 64) and cut disclaimers, but here only 1 refusal was dropped and disclaimers rose (10.9% vs 7.8%). Fine-tune bias is the closest alternative, since its median divergence (7.2) fits 8 slightly better than quantization's 12.3±4. But fine-tune bias should add refusals (about 2.4 per 64) and produce extra curt or very short replies. Here 0 refusals were added and short replies matched the reference (1 vs 1). Mean length is also nearly unchanged (61.7 vs 62.0). Unchanged refusal, disclaimer and stage-direction rates with a reworded-but-similar text profile best match quantization. Confidence is moderate because logit and activation data are missing.
